rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with an expanded blastocyst and visible ICM, but it overstates certainty about TE cohesion and suggests full-to-hatching features not clearly evident in this single somewhat blurry image.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, PCOS, prior biochemical pregnancies, semen parameters, BMI, and endometrium well with embryo quality, though some links (e.g., PCOS to aneuploidy) are somewhat speculative.
Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with conclusions broadly supported by embryo grade and patient factors; minor overinterpretation of morphology and prognosis prevents a top score.

Recommendations are largely consistent with standard IVF practice, including single embryo transfer and consideration of uterine/luteal review after repeated biochemical losses; PGT-A suggestion is somewhat stronger than guideline-based evidence for this profile.

Provides practical next steps for transfer management and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support review, possible uterine evaluation, and future protocol considerations, though some advice remains general rather than protocol-specific.
